wu: Warm-up: 'Clothes Line' — Students form a line, teacher calls out a clothing item, students race to grab a flashcard and line up holding it. Teacher asks 'What is this?' and students reply 'It's a T-shirt'.
wuAlt: Alternative 1: 'I Spy' — Teacher says 'I spy something blue', students guess clothing items.
Alternative 2: 'Mime the Item' — Student mimes a clothing item, classmates guess 'Are you a jacket?'
pres: Presentation: Use real clothes (T-shirt, jeans, dress) and flashcards. Teacher holds up items and says 'This is a red T-shirt. That is a blue dress'. Drill 'this/that/these/those' with students pointing. Ask 'What color is this?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Alternative 1: 'Fashion Show' — Teacher models clothes with exaggerated poses, students repeat vocabulary.
Alternative 2: 'Price Tag Game' — Stick price tags on items, teach 'How much is this?' with fake coins.
prac: Guided practice: 'This/That Auction' — Students in pairs bid on flashcards using 'This/That is... dollars'. Teacher gives fake money, highest bidder wins. Support with price lists and sentence frames.
pracAlt: Alternative 1: 'Color Match' — Students match clothing flashcards to color cards, saying 'This is a green shirt'.
Alternative 2: 'Size Drill' — Hold up size flashcards (S/M/L), students repeat 'This is small'.
ls: Listening slot: Play a dialogue from the 'Listening folder' (shop assistant asking 'What size?' and customer replying 'Medium'). Students listen and circle the correct size on a worksheet.
re: Reactivation game: 'Clothes Relay' — Two lines of students race to dress a mannequin with paper clothes, shouting 'This is a hat!' as they run.
prod: Production task: 'Shop Roleplay Rotation' — Students rotate as shopkeeper/ customer using price lists. Shopkeeper asks 'Can I help you?' Customer replies 'How much are these jeans?' and 'I'll take this'.
rw: Reading and writing slot: Read a simple shop ad with prices (e.g., 'T-shirts: $10'). Students answer 'How much is the T-shirt?' in notebooks. Then write a 6-line dialogue for homework.
st: Story + goodbye: Read 'The New Dress' story, then close with 'Today we learned to shop for clothes. Thank you, class!'
g: Students bid on flashcards using 'This/That is... dollars'
Race to dress a mannequin with paper clothes
Rotate as shopkeeper/customer with price lists
Match clothes flashcards to color cards
Hold up size flashcards and repeat 'This is small'
diff: Fast finishers: Design a dream outfit and write prices.
Support: Use sentence frames for dialogue (e.g., 'How much is ___?')
hw: Homework 2: Draw 5 clothes items and label them in English
Homework 3: Ask family about clothes prices and write 3 sentences
tip: Use realia (clothes) to make shopping vocabulary tangible for Moroccan teens, linking to local markets like souks.
